tests.test: chi-squared goodness-of-fit vs proportional to corpus

claims.interpretation: Gate-passer tradition distribution is significantly different from uniform (chi2=64.96, p=1.144e-12, V=0.526) and significantly different from corpus proportions (chi2=21.84, p=0.0005618, V=0.305).

claims.claim_text: Knowledge-reasoning conflation: most benchmarks test knowledge, not reasoning
claims.interpretation: Only 13/47 (27.7%) gate-passers test genuine theological reasoning. Binomial test confirms this is significantly below 50% (p=0.001544). 95% CI for reasoning proportion: [0.000, 0.403].

claims.claim_text: Data availability bottleneck: many benchmarks have unavailable data
claims.test: exact binomial test on accessibility rate
claims.interpretation: Overall, 231/401 (57.6%) entries have available data. Among gate-passers, 47/47 (100.0%) are accessible (p=7.105e-15, 95% CI [0.938, 1.000]). The 170 unavailable entries confirm a substantial data bottleneck.

claims.claim_text: Structural epistemic injustice: gate-passage correlates with Western proximity
claims.interpretation: Logistic regression (pseudo R²=0.068). family_African/Indigenous: OR=None, p=1.0 (not significant); family_Dharmic: OR=0.938471, p=0.861619 (not significant); family_East Asian: OR=0.398405, p=0.381292 (not significant); family_Other: OR=None, p=0.999998 (not significant); family_Unknown: OR=None, p=1.0 (not significant); P10_english: OR=1.758547, p=0.097163 (not significant); venue_tier: OR=1.339822, p=0.147558 (not significant).

claims.test: one-sample proportion test (binomial) + bootstrap median CI
claims.interpretation: 28/47 (59.6%) gate-passers are from 2024+. This is significantly above 50% (p=0.1215). Median year: 2024 (95% bootstrap CI: [2023, 2024]).

claims.claim_text: WEIRD bias: benchmarks from WEIRD contexts disproportionately pass gates
claims.test: Fisher's exact test (WEIRD approximated by English-language)
claims.interpretation: WEIRD (English-language) pass rate: 17/192 (8.9%); non-WEIRD: 30/209 (14.4%). Fisher's exact OR=0.580, p=0.09036. Not significant difference in gate-passage by WEIRD status.
claims.caveat: WEIRD status approximated from P10_language field. True author nationality would be more precise.

claims.claim_text: Bias-values conflation: many benchmarks detect bias rather than measure values alignment
claims.test: binomial test on bias vs values proportion (among non-mixed)
claims.interpretation: Among gate-passers: 10 bias-adjacent, 13 values-focused, 24 mixed. Among pure classifications (23 total), bias proportion = 10/23 (p=0.6776). The majority (24/47) are mixed theological-values, suggesting the field has not cleanly separated bias detection from values alignment.
